explanation: Age filter is birth_date <= '2026-09-24' AND birth_date > date('2026-09-24','-26 years'): selects every customer aged 0 to 25 instead of exactly 25 (completed age); no '= 25' condition, so the value is too high.

Period filter is correct, but the age filter is birth_date <= '2026-09-25' AND birth_date > date('2026-09-25','-26 years'): customers aged 0 to 25 instead of exactly 25 (same error as C08), so the value is too high.

Age is computed from month-day only, never from the birth year; the two month-day conditions are contradictory (mmdd <= '09-25' AND mmdd > mmdd||'-01-01' is always false as text), so no customer matches and the value is 0.

Age approximated as CAST(('2026-09-26' - birth_date)/365 AS INTEGER) = 25: in SQLite the text subtraction keeps only the leading year (2026 - 2001 = 25), then 25/365 = 0 in integer division, so the condition 0 = 25 is never true and the value is 0.

No 'age = 25' condition at all (only 'birthday this year <= order date < next birthday'); in addition '+' || N + 1 || ' years' evaluates to the number N+1 because || binds tighter than +, so strftime returns NULL and no line matches: value 0.

Products and period are correct, but the birth date is cut at the wrong positions: substr(birth_date,7,4) gives '9-25' (read as 9), so the age is about 2026 - 9 = 2017, and the month-day test builds '09-2001' instead of '09-25'; no customer reaches age 25: value 0.

Period is correct, but the age rule 'birth year + 25 <= order year' has no upper bound (customers older than 25 are kept; the OR branch '= year' is a subset), and substr(birth_date,7,2) gives '9-' so the month-day becomes '09-9-' instead of '09-25': value too high.
The returned SQL uses the C-style ternary operator '? :' (strftime(...) <= '12-01' ? '0 months' : '-1 month'), which does not exist in SQLite: syntax error, the query is not executed, no value.
